property_summary: In the reference contract, setL1BlockValues never changes any state, so c.basefee() remains 0 after every admissible call; the mutant stores _basefee, so for any call with a nonzero _basefee (reachable since anyone can pass a nonzero value even though the require reverts only for non-depositors) — note here the depositorAccount check makes both revert for non-depositors, so the fuzzer must call from a non-depositor and expect revert, but for depositor the mutant writes: the general rule 'c.basefee() == 0 after any successful setL1BlockValues' is broken by the mutant for nonzero _basefee.
For any caller that is not DEPOSITOR_ACCOUNT, setL1BlockValues succeeds (depositorAccount defaults to address(0)); the mutant wrongly reverts for such callers.

Any call to setL1BlockValues with a sender other than the depositor account must revert and never mutate state; the mutant inserts state writes after the require, so when msg.sender equals the (zero) depositor account it wrongly succeeds and stores the parameters, breaking the rule for some inputs.
setL1BlockValues must revert when called by an address other than the depositor account (observable as a revert boolean for a non-depositor caller).
